accessTokenHint: The token the device presents. Generate one or paste your own.
cancelHeldConfirmBody_one: Cancel the {{count}} command held for this device? It will not be sent, even after the device is enabled. A command already sent cannot be recalled.
cancelHeldConfirmBody_other: Cancel the {{count}} commands held for this device? They will not be sent, even after the device is enabled. A command already sent cannot be recalled.
commandFromBatchHint: One batch sent this command to many devices at once. Open it to see the whole write — including the devices it refused, which received nothing and have no command row anywhere.
commandHint: The commands this device's published profile declares.
commandIssueFailed: Couldn’t issue the command. Try again.
commandNameHint: The command the device knows how to handle.
commandNotCancelled: Command “{{name}}” wasn’t cancelled — it had already moved on to {{status}}
countExceedsMax: Count cannot exceed {{max}} per bulk create.
credentialTypeHint: How the device proves its identity.
deleteCredentialConfirm: Delete this {{credentialType}} credential? The device can no longer authenticate with it.
deviceTypeBatchHint: Every device in the batch gets this type.
disableDeviceConfirm: Disable “{{token}}”? Its events will be discarded instead of stored, it cannot open a new connection, and commands to it will be refused. Commands already queued for it are held until you enable it again. A connection it already has stays open until it ends. Its data, credentials and configuration are kept, and you can enable it again at any time.
enableDeviceConfirm: Enable “{{token}}”? Its events will be stored again and it can connect and receive commands. Events it sent while disabled were discarded and do not come back.
externalIdTemplateHint: Optional business id. Supports {n}, {n:0Wd}, and {random} for a random id per device.
externalIdTemplateNeedsVariation: External ID template must include {n}, {n:0Wd} or {random} when creating more than one device.
heldWhileDisabled_one: {{count}} queued command held while this device is disabled
heldWhileDisabled_other: {{count}} queued commands held while this device is disabled
heldWhileDisabledHint: They are not sent and not cancelled. They go out, oldest first, when the device is enabled, or lapse at their own expiry time.
locationNoPermission: You don’t have permission to view this device’s location.
nameTemplateNoRandom: Name template must not use {random}; it is only meaningful for external IDs.
noAssignments: This device is not assigned. Its telemetry still flows — assign it to give its events a customer/area/asset anchor.
noCommandsDeclaredHint: This device's profile declares no commands, so any command name is accepted. Declare commands on its device profile — and publish it — to get a typed form here.
noCommandsIssued: No commands have been issued to this device yet.
noCredentials: No credentials registered for this device yet.
noEvents: No events received from this device yet.
noLocationRecorded: This device has not reported a position.
noMeasurements: No measurements received from this device yet.
noStateRecorded: No state recorded for this device yet.
passwordHint: Shown once, right after you add the credential. The platform keeps only a one-way digest, so it can never be shown again.
passwordIsSet: Password is set. It cannot be shown.
passwordShownOnce: Copy it now. You won't see this password again; the old one no longer works.
passwordTooShort: Shorter than {{min}} bytes. The platform refuses passwords under {{min}} bytes (counted as UTF-8, so non-Latin characters take more than one).
rotateWarning: The device's current password stops working as soon as you save.
payloadFreeformHint: Optional. Sent to the device verbatim (e.g. JSON).
payloadStructuredHint: This command declares a structured parameter, so its payload is entered as JSON.
quietPresenceBody: Nothing has reported this device as disconnected — it simply has not sent anything recently, which is also what a healthy device on a slow reporting interval looks like. Check the Commands tab to see how commands to it are actually faring.
renderedTokenInvalid: Rendered token “{{token}}” is not valid: use letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
startIndexMustBePositive: Start index must be a whole number ≥ 1.
structuredParameterHint: Structured parameter — send this command with a raw payload instead.
title: Devices
tokenTemplateHint: Must include {n} or {n:0Wd} (zero-padded to width W).
tokenTemplateNeedsIndex: Token template must contain an {n} placeholder so every device gets a distinct token.
tokenTemplateNoRandom: Token template must not use {random}; use {n} or {n:0Wd} so tokens are reproducible.
typeIdentityIntro: Manufacturer and model identify the physical device. They are discovery facets — used to filter and group — so the fields suggest values already in use to keep them consistent, while still letting you type a new one.
typeProfileCapabilityLimitedBody: Devices of this type are still classified and displayed, but report no typed metrics, accept no commands, and raise no alarms until a profile is attached.
typeProfileCreate: Create a profile for this type
typeProfileDetachConfirm: Detach “{{token}}” from this device type? Its devices keep working but lose their typed capabilities — no metric typing, commands, or alarms — until a profile is re-attached. The profile itself is not deleted.
typeProfileIntro: A profile is the reusable capability contract — metrics, commands, detection rules, and configuration and position declarations — that this device type adopts. Authoring lives on the profile; here you choose which one this type uses.
typeProfileLoadError: Couldn’t load the profiles to choose from. You can still create one below.
typeProfileNoPermission: You don’t have permission to change this type’s profile.
typeProfileShared: Shared by {{count}} device types — changes to its definitions affect all of them.
vocabularyUnavailableHint: Couldn't read this device's commands, so its declared vocabulary isn't shown. Anything you send is still checked by the server.
replaceDeviceConfirm: Every credential the current unit can authenticate with is disabled, and a new credential is issued for the replacement unit. The device keeps its identity, history, alarms and assignments. This cannot be undone from here.
replaceDeviceHint: Bind a new physical unit to this device. Its identity, external id, type, history, alarms, assignments and group membership all carry forward — only the credentials change.
replacementReasonHint: Why the unit was replaced. Recorded on the maintenance history.
newUnitIdentifierHint: The incoming hardware's own serial or IMEI. Recorded on the history; the device's external id is not changed.
newUnitCredentialHint: Shown once. Copy it now — it cannot be read back from the maintenance history.
noReplacements: This device has never been replaced.
configurationDeviceNotFound: No configuration is available for this device.
configPendingBody: The device last reported revision #{{reported}}; revision #{{desired}} is waiting to be applied.
configPendingNeverReported: Revision #{{desired}} is waiting to be applied; the device has not reported a revision.
configStaleBody: The values the device's profile and shared attributes would produce now differ from the latest revision. A newer revision is created when a declared key is next written or the device next synchronizes.
configDeclaredKeysHint: Shown from the profile's active published version. Values are edited as shared attributes in the Facets tab; changing a declared key creates a new revision.
configDeclarationUnavailable: The profile's declaration could not be read.
configNoDeclaredKeys: This device's profile declares no configuration keys, so the device sees an empty document.
configInvalidHint: Keys marked invalid hold a value that cannot be carried as the declared type and are left out of the document.
configUndeclaredHint: These shared attributes are not named by the declaration, so they are never sent to the device.
configNoRevisionBody: No configuration revision has been created for this device yet.
configCopyHint: Preview the latest configuration of another device in this tenant, then apply it here. This device's profile must declare every key it carries.
configCopyNoRevision: Device “{{token}}” has no configuration revision to copy.
configPreviewHint_one: Applying changes {{count}} key. It creates a new revision and sends it to the device; earlier revisions are kept unchanged.
configPreviewHint_other: Applying changes {{count}} keys. It creates a new revision and sends it to the device; earlier revisions are kept unchanged.
configPreviewNoChanges: The device already holds this configuration; there is nothing to apply.
importModeHint_NONE: Create the devices only. Add credentials afterwards.
importModeHint_FACTORY_CREDENTIALS: Create each device together with the credential your factory supplied for it, in one step.
importPickHint: A CSV file up to {{maxMb}} MiB and {{maxRows}} rows, with a header row. UTF-8; comma, semicolon or tab separated.
importFileTypeLabel: Device type for the whole file
importFileTypeHint: Used for every row whose type column is empty or not mapped.
importPreviewTitle: First rows as they will be sent
importSecretsNotice: Secrets are sent once, are never shown or written to the results, and are cleared from this page when the import ends. The file itself stays your responsibility.
importNeedsType: Map a device type column or choose a device type for the whole file.
importNeedsCredentialColumns: Map the credential type and credential id columns.
importNothingToCreate: Nothing in this file would be created. Fix the rows listed above, or download the results.
importStopped_one: Stopped after {{count}} row. Importing the same file again continues where this left off.
importStopped_other: Stopped after {{count}} rows. Importing the same file again continues where this left off.
importChunkFailed: The import stopped after {{count}} rows: {{error}} Importing the same file again continues where this left off.
importRerunHint: Fix the rows that need attention in the failed-rows file and import it again. Devices that were created are reported as already existing and left alone.
importShowingFirst: Showing the first {{shown}} of {{total}}. Download the results for the rest.
importErr_too_large: That file is larger than {{maxMb}} MiB. Split it and import the parts.
importErr_invalid_utf8: That file is not UTF-8 text. In your spreadsheet, save it as “CSV UTF-8”.
importErr_too_many_rows: That file has more than {{maxRows}} rows. Split it and import the parts.
importErr_unterminated_quote: A quoted value in that file is never closed. Check for a stray quotation mark.
updDeviceDisabled: This device is disabled, so it is cut off from updates.
updDeviceDisabledHint: No new update can be assigned until it is enabled again. Disabling the device does not recall an update already in flight; cancel it below if it should not proceed. A queued update is cancelled at once, but one the device has already picked up stays cancel-pending while the device is disabled, because its reports are refused: it completes once the device is enabled again and confirms, or ends as timed out at the stage deadline.
updNoCurrent: No update is assigned to this device.
updNoHistory: This device has no update history.
updSignerError: Could not read the pinned signer: {{message}}
updNoPin: None. This assignment pins no signature.
updSignerRevokedNote: Revoked after assignment; the pin does not move, so this update keeps the signature it was assigned under.
updFailureExplain_SIGNATURE_INVALID: The device checked the artifact signature and it did not verify against the key the device holds, so it refused to install.
updFailureExplain_UNKNOWN_SIGNER: The device does not hold the key that signed this artifact, or it requires a signature and this assignment is unverified, so it refused to install. Provision the signer key on the device.
updFailureExplain_VERIFICATION_FAILED: The bytes the device downloaded do not match the artifact digest, so it refused to install. The download was damaged or incomplete; assign the update again.
updUnknownExplain: The update was running or rebooting when the device stopped reporting, so its outcome is not known. The device may be on either version. It stays in this state until the device reports its inventory, or until you abandon it.
updBeyondRecall: Installation has begun, so this update can no longer be cancelled.
updCancelConfirmQueued: The update has not reached the device yet and is cancelled immediately. The device is told, and a new update can be assigned afterwards.
updCancelConfirmRequested: The device is told to stop. The cancel completes only when the device confirms it; until then the update stays in its current state with a cancel pending. Once installation has begun it can no longer be cancelled.
updCancelRequested: Cancel requested. It completes when the device confirms.
updAbandonConfirm: The update ends as cancelled with your reason recorded, the change is journaled under your name, and the device is sent a cancel. This frees the device for a new assignment. It does not find out what the device runs: it may be on either version, so check its inventory before relying on either.
updReasonHint: Required. It is kept on the update.
updReasonRequired: A reason is required to abandon an update.
updArtifactHint: Only available artifacts are listed. The device profile must be on the artifact’s compatible list.
updUnverifiedBlocked: This artifact is unverified, and this instance does not allow assigning unverified artifacts. Sign it with a registered signer first.
updLiveBlocksAssign: This device already has an update in progress. Assigning another is refused until that one is cancelled or finishes.
updAssignDisabledHint: Assigning is unavailable while the device is disabled.
connectIntro: Run one of these commands to send this device its first measurement, then look for it on the Events tab. They are built from this device's credential and its profile's published metrics.
connectShell: The commands are written for a POSIX shell such as bash or zsh. On Windows, run them in WSL or Git Bash: PowerShell and cmd.exe read the quoting and the line breaks differently, and the command would not send what it shows.
connectDisabledBody: Events from a disabled device are discarded when they arrive, and the sender is not told. Enable the device before you send it data.
connectNoCredentialBody: A device presents a credential on its connection and on every event, and an event without one is refused. Add an enabled credential on the Credentials tab. A disabled or expired credential does not count.
connectCopyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard
connectPlaceholderInstance: Replace {{placeholder}} with the instance id chosen when the instance was installed. It is also the instance's Kubernetes namespace without its dci- prefix.
connectPlaceholderMqttHost: Replace {{placeholder}} with the host your operator exposes the MQTT listener on. The listener uses TLS: save the instance CA certificate as {{ca}}.
connectMqttClientId: Keep the client id (-i) as shown. The broker refuses any other, including the random one a client library picks when none is set.
connectPlaceholderIngestHost: Replace {{placeholder}} with the host of the HTTP ingest listener. It is not exposed outside the cluster by default; for a quick test, forward port 8081 of the event-sources service.
connectPlaceholderPassword: Replace {{placeholder}} with this credential's password, in both places. It was shown once, when it was set, and cannot be shown again. If it is lost, set a new one on the Credentials tab.
connectExamplePublished: The example readings use the metrics in the profile's published version, with values it accepts.
connectExamplePartial_one: The example readings use the metrics in the profile's published version, with values it accepts. {{count}} more metric is left out to keep the command short.
connectExamplePartial_other: The example readings use the metrics in the profile's published version, with values it accepts. {{count}} more metrics are left out to keep the command short.
connectExampleFallback: The profile's published version has no metric this example can use, so it sends an undeclared reading. An undeclared reading is stored as long as its value is a number.
connectAcceptedIsNotStored: A 202 response or an MQTT acknowledgement means the event was received, not that it was stored. Check the Events tab to see that it arrived.
gatewayHint: A gateway is a device that fronts other devices, such as the agent at a site. Its credential publishes for the devices behind it on its own topics; a publish for a device that is not assigned to it is refused and recorded in failed events. Assigning a gateway gives it the same standing over a device as issuing the device a credential.
gatewayNone: This device is not behind a gateway.
gatewayChooseFirst: Enter the token of the gateway device.
gatewayClearConfirm: Take this device out from behind gateway “{{token}}”? The gateway’s next publish for it is refused and recorded in failed events.
gatewayNoChildren: No devices are assigned to this device as their gateway.
